First listed 2026-01-30 · episode or wrap

Silver Goes Crazy, United Healthcare is Falling, & AI’s CapEx is Exploding | The Weekly Wrap

Eisman contrasts resilient stocks with metals speculation, argues physical silver tightness may matter, and sees possible broader fiscal-led growth. He warns UnitedHealth requires a deep repair and forecasts 2027 EPS below $19, conditional on weak Medicare pricing. That earnings horizon remains open and final CMS pricing later improved. He favors power bottlenecks, distinguishes supplier growth from AI customer returns, and identifies real Microsoft backlog concentration. His silver explanation overstates the novelty of China exporter controls and leaves key quantities unverified.

How he reasons here

  • Compare different markets rather than infer universal sentiment from VIX.
  • Differentiate superficial turnarounds from structural business repairs.
  • Use sector-specific operating metrics such as orders or comparable sales.
